title: Dashboard Widgets picker lists two different widgets both called "Guiding"
reasoning: Reproduced live on the rebuilt bundle (profile v2-wizards, display :87). Dashboard -> Edit Dashboard -> Widgets, scrolling the list with the wheel, the a11y tree reports 'check box: Guiding' twice in the SAME dialog: once in the cockpit block (between 'Equipment Telemetry' and 'Weather & Safety') and again ~14 rows later in the legacy block (between 'Sequence Status' and 'Equipment'). The same dialog also lists 'Weather & Safety' and 'Weather', and 'Equipment Telemetry' and 'Equipment'. Source confirms the cause exactly as claimed: widget_picker_dialog.dart:71-101 iterates the whole dashboardWidgetRegistry and renders definition.title verbatim, and dashboard_widget_registry.dart has id: cockpitGuiding title 'Guiding' subtitle 'RMS error and guiding graph' (line 162-169) and id: guiding title 'Guiding' subtitle 'RMS and guiding graph' (line 337-344) - the two subtitles quoted in the finding are verbatim correct. 'where' is accurate.

title: Glance mode toggle on the Dashboard changes nothing on the Dashboard
location_wrong: The finding's supporting claim that neither glanceStyle consumer 'is on the Dashboard screen' is FALSE. dashboard_widget_registry.dart registers BOTH of them as dashboard tiles: cockpitFilterIntegration -> _buildCockpitFilterIntegration -> RunDashboardFilterIntegration (registry lines ~143-151 / 471-477) and cockpitSessionWarnings -> _buildCockpitSessionWarnings -> RunDashboardSessionWarningsPanel (~180-187 / 503-509). They ARE on the Dashboard; they just render nothing outside an active run. The correct 'where' is glance_mode_toggle.dart (the control) + the fact that only those two run-scoped panels opt in, not the always-visible status readouts.
reasoning: Symptom reproduced on the rebuilt bundle. Dashboard with the sim camera + sim mount connected (cockpit awake, Filter Integration / Session Warnings / Mount Control tiles enabled). Captured full-res before and after clicking the eye toggle; a11y tree confirms the state flipped ('Glance mode [off]' -> 'Glance mode [ON]'). Pixel diff of the two 1920x1200 captures shows changes ONLY in the command bar (the toggle chip + the ticking clock, y 228-260) and in the right rail at x 1520-1677 - and a control diff of two captures taken 5 s apart in the SAME glance state shows the identical right-rail drift (live heartbeat events / sensor temp). No text anywhere on the dashboard changed size. Source explains why: session_warnings_panel.dart returns SizedBox.shrink() when warnings are empty, and filter_integration_panel.dart only emits its glanceStyle text per configured filter - so with no run there is nothing glance-styled on screen at all, and the header readouts the tooltip implies (Temp/Focus/HFR/RMS/target) never call glanceStyle. Downgraded to P3: it is a misleading affordance, not a data or safety issue, and it does have a real (if narrow) effect during a run with warnings/filters.

title: Dashboard Mount jog pad fires a 500 ms pulse guide instead of a slew - the arrows do nothing a user can see
reasoning: Reproduced exactly on the rebuilt bundle. Dashboard -> Edit Dashboard -> Widgets -> Mount Control -> Done, sim mount connected, Unpark, then one click on the E chevron produced a single native log line '2026-08-03T20:48:05 INFO Pulse guiding sim_mount_1 for 500ms in direction east' and the card's RA stayed '00h 00m 00s' / Dec '+00d 00' 00"'. Press-and-hold (xdotool mousedown, 2.5 s, mouseup) produced EXACTLY ONE further 500 ms pulse, not a continuous slew - verified by counting 'Pulse guiding' lines appended to /tmp/ns-audit/v2-wizards/app.log across the hold. 'where' is accurate: mount_control_card.dart:173-182 is the _MountDirectionalPad construction, with line 176 'onDirection: (direction) async {' and line 179 '.pulseGuide(direction);'. mount_command_service.dart:375 declares 'Future<CommandActionResult> pulseGuide(String direction, {int durationMs = 500})' and the card never passes a duration, so every arrow press is the 500 ms default. Severity P2 stands.

title: Mount jog arrows are silently dead while the mount is parked
reasoning: Reproduced. With the sim mount reporting Parked, clicking the E chevron and then the N chevron appended ZERO new lines to /tmp/ns-audit/v2-wizards/app.log (line count unchanged at 97), no snackbar/alert appeared in the a11y tree, and RA stayed 00:00:00. After Unpark the very same click produced 'Pulse guiding ... east' immediately, so the pad really was inert only because of the parked gate. The cited lines are exact: mount_control_card.dart:175 is 'isEnabled: isConnected && !mountState.isParked,' and :413 is 'onTap: isEnabled ? onPressed : null,' (InkWell opens on :412). The disabled affordance claim also holds structurally - _DirectionalButton keeps Material(color: colors.surfaceAlt) in both states and changes only the Icon colour (textPrimary -> textMuted, :419-421), so there is no container/opacity change to signal 'disabled'. Severity P3 stands.

title: The Smart Night dashboard prompt never appears even with its toggle on and every documented precondition met
reasoning: Reproduced on the rebuilt bundle and root-caused. Setup on a fresh v2-wizards profile: Settings -> Location lat 40.0 / lon -105.0 (verified in the scratch DB: app_settings observer_latitude=40.0, observer_longitude=-105.0), Equipment -> Edit Profile focal length 550 / aperture 100 (verified: equipment_profiles row 1|My Equipment|550.0|100.0), sim camera + sim mount connected, no sequence running, nothing dismissed, smartNightAutoPromptEnabled defaults to true (app_settings.dart:384 '@Default(true) bool smartNightAutoPromptEnabled'). Sat on the dashboard for >4.5 minutes; the a11y tree never contained 'Hardware ready' or 'Smart Night will choose' at any point. ROOT CAUSE (sharper than the finding's two hypotheses, one of which it named): smart_night_prompt_card.dart:21 declares 'final smartNightPromptNowProvider = Provider<DateTime>((ref) => DateTime.now());' - a NON-autoDispose Riverpod Provider, so DateTime.now() is evaluated once and cached for the container's life. _equipmentReadyGraceElapsed (:297-326) then does '_equipmentReadySince ??= now' and 'final elapsed = now.difference(_equipmentReadySince!)', which is therefore ALWAYS Duration.zero. elapsed never reaches the 60 s grace, so readyGraceElapsed is permanently false, canPlan (:118-122) is permanently false, and the card returns SizedBox.shrink() forever. The 60 s _graceTimer fires once, setState rebuilds, elapsed is still zero, and because _graceTimer is left non-null the '??=' never re-arms it. The 'where' (smart_night_prompt_card.dart:118-144) is accurate - :118-127 is exactly the canPlan/baseShouldShow block and :139-144 is exactly the draftAsync guard. Severity P2 stands.

title: The same mosaic is described as "3x2 grid" on one screen and "2x3 grid" on the other
reasoning: Confirmed by exact source inspection on the rebuilt tree; the two formatters really do transpose. mosaic_project_screen.dart:470 emits "'${project.cols}x${project.rows} grid'" and mosaic_projects_list_screen.dart:152 emits the identical "'${project.cols}x${project.rows} grid  .  '" - COLS FIRST. collaborative_sky/widgets/collab_mosaic_card.dart:86 emits "'${mosaic.rows}x${mosaic.cols} grid . '" (with a U+00D7 multiplication sign) - ROWS FIRST. So a project stored rows=2, cols=3 renders '3x2 grid' on both mosaic screens and '2x3 grid' on the Collaborate card, exactly as reported, and neither string states which axis is which. The finding's 'where' is right in substance; the precise collaborative-side line is collab_mosaic_card.dart:86, not the screen file. Not driven end-to-end in the GUI (would require standing up a hub, publishing and re-browsing), but the strings are unconditional literals with no branch that could make them agree.

title: The mosaic project screen's back breadcrumb always says "Mosaic projects" even when it returns somewhere else
reasoning: Confirmed by source on the rebuilt tree. mosaic_project_screen.dart:426-430 renders a bare 'Mosaic projects' string literal next to the back IconButton - there is no parameter, provider or route inspection feeding it. The button's handler _leave (:439-446) is 'if (navigator.canPop()) { navigator.pop(); return; } context.go('/mosaic');' - i.e. it pops to whatever is underneath, and only falls back to the projects list when the stack is empty. The claimed entry path is real: collab_mosaic_detail_screen.dart:386-390 does 'await navigator.push(MaterialPageRoute(builder: (_) => MosaicProjectScreen(projectId: projectId)))' after Join mosaic, so the route underneath is the Collaborative-Sky mosaic detail and the breadcrumb labelled 'Mosaic projects' returns there. 'where' is accurate. Severity P3 stands.

title: "Save Location Required" dialog's Continue button silently does nothing when no folder is chosen
reasoning: ALREADY FIXED in the rebuilt bundle. save_path_dialog.dart now wires the button as 'onPressed: _pathController.text.isNotEmpty ? _confirm : null' (the Actions row at the end of build), and initState registers '_pathController.addListener(_handlePathChanged)' whose only job is 'if (mounted) setState(() {});' - so the button's enabled state tracks the field live. Verified in the running app: Imaging -> Camera tab -> Flat Wizard -> Start Capture opened 'Save Location Required' with the field empty; the Continue button's fill measured mean RGB (31,36,42) - i.e. the dialog surface colour, unmistakably the disabled treatment next to the primary-blue 'Start Capture' behind it. Typing '/tmp/ns-audit/flats' into the field flipped the same 70x31 px region to mean RGB (86,149,186), full primary blue. So the button is neither clickable-but-inert nor 'at full primary contrast'; both halves of the reported symptom are gone. Residual nit (not the reported defect): the disabled state still carries no explanatory hint text.

title: Flat wizard's "Flat capture failed - no frames were saved" gives no reason and no next step
reasoning: Reproduced verbatim on the rebuilt bundle and root-caused. Setup: sim camera + sim filter wheel connected, Imaging -> Camera tab -> Flat Wizard -> Quick Capture, filter R, target 50% (~32768 ADU), tolerance +/-10%, Start Capture. The run ramped exposure 2.39s (ADU 1049) -> 13.79s (ADU 1198) -> 30.00s (ADU 1364) and stopped with the header 'EXPOSURE 30.00s ADU 1364 FRAME 0/30', status chip 'Failed' and the red banner 'Flat capture failed - no frames were saved.' - within 3 ADU of the finding's reported 1361. I then grepped the ENTIRE a11y tree for 'max exposure', 'under target', 'panel brightness' and 'converge': the only hit was the chart title 'ADU Convergence'. Nothing on screen states the reason. ROOT CAUSE, sharper than the finding: the reason IS computed and IS stored, but has no reader. flat_wizard_service.dart:1136 returns errorMessage 'Max exposure reached but still under target' (siblings at :1148 'Min exposure reached but still over target' and :1160 'Did not converge within N iterations'), and flat_wizard_provider.dart:1019-1023 does setWarningMessage('${filterName}: ${calibration.errorMessage}') - but grep shows NO widget under packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/flat_wizard/ ever reads state.warningMessage; the only message the UI renders is state.errorMessage (action_buttons.dart:17 'if (state.errorMessage != null)' and :32 'state.errorMessage!'), which _setFinalStatus (flat_wizard_provider.dart:1310-1311) sets to the generic literal 'Flat capture failed - no frames were saved.'. The finding's 'where' is right and the fix is a one-line surface: render warningMessage next to errorMessage. Severity P2 stands.

title: All-Sky reticle labels collide: the error marker, the az/alt caption and the "Dn" compass label are drawn on top of each other
reasoning: Confirmed by exact geometry in the cited file - and the cited file is right: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/polar_alignment/widgets/all_sky_target_reticle.dart. Inside one SizedBox(size, size) Stack: (1) the numeric caption Column is 'Positioned(bottom: 8, left: 0, right: 0)' (:92-95) holding a 22px total-error Text and, directly under it, the 11px 'Az ... Alt ...' Text (:112-125) - so the az/alt line occupies roughly y = size-22 .. size-8, centred. (2) _drawCardinal for Alignment.bottomCenter (:222, :351-354) places 'Dn' at 'center.dy + radius + padding' with radius = min(w,h)/2 - 16 and padding = 4, i.e. its top edge at y = size - 12, centred on the same x - it lands INSIDE the caption's band and even runs a pixel past the bottom edge. (3) the marker dot (:304-307, r = 6) is drawn from the az/alt offset clamped to maxRadius, so an altitude-dominated error like the reported Alt -1765.4" of a 1800" total pins it to bottom-centre at y = size-16 - the same band again, and because the caption is a later Stack child it paints OVER the dot, exactly matching the reported 'dot bisects the -351.4 text'. Three elements, one ~30px bottom-centre band, by construction and with no guard. Not driven live: reaching a completed All-Sky result needs a plate solve and this scratch profile reports 'No plate solver is configured', so I verified it from the layout arithmetic rather than a screenshot - hence P3 rather than a stronger claim. Severity P3 stands.

title: Collaborative Sky dialogs render inside an empty full-height slab
location_wrong: The real defect is NOT 'collaborative_sky/ dialog scaffolding' - it is a nested-dialog mismatch between a shared UI helper and three sheet bodies, one of which lives outside that directory. showAdaptiveModal's desktop branch (packages/skotiq_ui/lib/src/layout/adaptive_modal.dart:102-127) ALREADY wraps the body in a Material Dialog painted colors.surface, sized 'SizedBox(width: size.width, height: size.height)' where AdaptiveDialogConstraints.dialogSize returns height: NULL when the caller omits designHeight (adaptive_dialog_constraints.dart:46-48). The three offending bodies then return a SECOND dialog: constellation_sign_in_sheet.dart:53, coimaging_create_sheet.dart:155 and mosaic_contribute_sheet.dart:196 each 'return SkotiqDialog(...)'. Fix belongs at those three call sites (or in showAdaptiveModal), not in the Collaborative Sky screen.
reasoning: Reproduced on the rebuilt bundle. Plan Tonight -> Discover -> Collaborate -> 'Connect to a hub'. The capture (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2w-34.png) shows a lighter slab spanning x 433-847 from y~20 to y~700 of the 720 px window, with the actual dialog card only at y 170-549 - roughly 150 px of empty surface above the title and 150 px below the buttons (the finding's 'roughly 300 px above' overstates it; everything else matches). Pixel sampling proves the slab is a real surface and not the scrim: inside the slab above the card = RGB (17,20,24), the dimmed page either side = (5,6,7), the dialog card = (24,28,34). Control case that isolates the cause: 'Name a region' (your_sky/widgets/name_region_sheet.dart:26) also calls showAdaptiveModal WITHOUT designHeight but does NOT return a SkotiqDialog, and it renders correctly wrapped (y 222-497, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2w-35.png) - so the slab is caused by the nested SkotiqDialog, not by showAdaptiveModal alone. Exactly the three dialogs the finding named are exactly the three showAdaptiveModal bodies that return SkotiqDialog. Severity P3 stands.

title: Collaborative Sky still says "No collaborative mosaics on this hub yet" right after you publish one
reasoning: Confirmed by source; could not be driven end-to-end because no skotiq_hub is running on this machine (/tmp/ns-audit/hub/ does not exist and no hub process is up), and standing one up was out of scope. The code is unambiguous. collaborative_sky_providers.dart:19 declares 'final collaborativeMosaicsProvider = FutureProvider<List<CollabMosaic>>((ref) { return ref.watch(collaborativeMosaicServiceProvider).listMosaics(); });' - NOT autoDispose, so its AsyncValue is cached for the container's life and survives leaving/re-entering the screen. Repo-wide there are exactly two non-test references to it: the watch at collaborative_sky_screen.dart:639 and a single invalidate at collaborative_sky_screen.dart:81, inside _refresh() - which is only the manual refresh icon in the screen header, exactly as the finding reported ('Pressing the refresh icon made it appear'). The publish path never touches it: mosaic_project_controller.dart:507-526 publishToHub() does 'await collaborative.publishProject(_projectId); await load();' where load() only reloads THIS controller's own project state. And the list is guaranteed to be warm-and-empty before the publish, because the Collaborative Sky screen is where the hub connection is made in the first place. 'where' is accurate. Severity P2 stands.
